one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event dominates the window: Q3 2026 results after the close on Tue 2026-10-20. Consensus is about $2.64 non-GAAP EPS on about $2.91B revenue. The comparison is tough: Q3 2025 da Vinci procedures grew ~19%, and its $2.40 EPS included a $0.12 tax benefit. H1 2026 da Vinci procedure growth was ~15.5% (16% Q1, 15% Q2), and the guide is 13.5-15.5% 'closer to the midpoint', which implies only ~13-14% in H2. Management also promised to quantify the 2027 Extended Use Program on this call. On the Q2 call BofA floated a ~5-point I&A-per-procedure impact spread over a couple of years (the 2020 program was modeled at ~7%). Management calls it 'directionally similar to 2020', with a 'gradual' net decline, so the sizing is more likely to land as a headwind than a relief. Against that, the 2020 precedent ended near -2%, and the Wells Fargo commentary (Sept 9) kept the outlook. New since round 1: the stock rallied from $350 (Sept 8) to $415 (Sept 28) on that commentary and the Sept 22 EU approvals, and closed $401 today. That removes the cushion the July low had given, and HCA's Q2 elective-surgery weakness argues against a US re-acceleration print. ISRG has beaten EPS consensus four quarters running, but the stock has fallen on two of the last prints despite beats. Net: a slight negative skew. I put the median at ~$398 with a monthly sigma of ~11.5% (37%/3.5 plus an earnings-gap premium), so P(>= spot) is 0.48. That is a small tilt, not a confident call.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%: 2028E non-GAAP EPS $13.3 x 31x = $412, what the market will price on NTM EPS in Oct-2027) and a 10-year FCF DCF (40%: normalized 2027 FCF $3.5B, 12.5%/8.5% growth, 8.5% WACC, 4% terminal, +$8.6B cash, 351M shares, rolled forward 12 months = ~$404).

methods.name: P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 actual $2.50 + $2.80 = $5.30 (Q2 included a ~$36M IEEPA tariff refund). H2 consensus is ~$5.48 (Q3 ~$2.64), for FY consensus $10.78. I add ~$0.12 for ISRG's record of four straight beats.

Consensus is $12.09-12.33 (low $11.05). I sit ~2-3% below it. The EUP is 'directionally similar' to 2020 (2020 modeled $150-170M, ~7% of I&A), and BofA's ~5-point framework phased over 2027-28 implies roughly a 2-3% I&A/procedure drag in 2027, i.e. ~$150-200M of high-margin revenue, ~$0.35-0.45/share. Mix (da Vinci 5, force feedback, SP) and buybacks only partly offset it.

2027E $11.9 grown ~12%: ~12% procedure growth, the remaining EUP drag, op-margin leverage (non-GAAP op margin ~41-42% vs a 35-40% target, so limited upside), and ~1% share shrink ($4.7B authorization left). That is below aggregator 2028 consensus of $13.91.

Today's $401 is ~33x 2027 consensus ($12.2). I trim to 31x for Oct-2027 because EPS growth decelerates toward low-teens, J&J Ottava (De Novo 2026-07-22) and Medtronic Hugo (general-surgery 510(k)s filed June 2026) enter US soft tissue, and the Ninth Circuit reversal in SIS raises aftermarket antitrust risk. I do not assume a return to the historical 45-55x.

Normalizing for the tax item gives ~25%. 2026 revenue ~$11.8B (consensus $11.76B) grown ~13% = ~$13.3B x ~26% = ~$3.5B.

da Vinci procedures went from +18% (2025) to a 13.5-15.5% guide (2026), H1 ~15.5%, implied H2 ~13-14%. Installed base +12%, Ion +36%, OUS +20%, US +12%. Low-teens for four years, fading as the base grows and EUP pricing bites.
Debt-free large-cap medtech. Cost of equity ~8.5% given 37% realized vol and the new litigation and competitive risk. 4% terminal for a franchise with a long procedure runway.

bear.story: US da Vinci growth slides to high single digits. ACA attrition (HCA: exchange admissions -15%, outpatient surgeries -3.4% same-facility in Q2) is compounded by Medicaid work requirements from 2027-01-01. The EUP is sized near BofA's ~5-point framework with little elasticity. SIS proceeds on remand, the hospital class trial (2027-09-14) looms, and remanufactured instruments gain share. Ottava and Hugo start lengthening selling cycles. 2028E EPS ~$12.0 at ~24.5x.

base.story: Procedures grow ~12-13% in 2027. The EUP trims I&A/procedure 2-3% in 2027, partly offset by da Vinci 5 mix, SP, Ion and buybacks. EPS ~$11.9 (2027) and ~$13.3 (2028E), multiple ~31x NTM. Litigation stays unresolved but not material within the horizon.

bull.story: Deferred procedures return (HCA expects 2027 coverage loss to be smaller than 2026). The EUP drives elasticity in benign and ASC procedures and lands near the 2020 outcome (~-2%). Cardiac, nipple-sparing mastectomy and the da Vinci 5 upgrade cycle (144 trade-ins in Q2 vs 83) keep growth near 15%. En banc rehearing helps in SIS. The market re-rates toward ~38x on ~$14.2 2028E.

thesis_break_reason: $300 is ~9% below the July 2026 low ($328.57) and ~25x 2027 consensus, below my 31x base even on a reduced EPS path. A trade there would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than 37%-vol noise. Candidates: an EUP sizing well beyond ~5 points or front-loaded into 2027, a 2027 procedure guide below ~11%, an adverse SIS/class-action development (the Ninth Circuit already revived SIS; the class trial is set for 2027-09-14) that forces open the EndoWrist aftermarket, or evidence that Ottava/Hugo are winning US general-surgery placements.

US procedure trajectory: HCA's Q2 outpatient surgeries -3.4% same-facility and inpatient elective -6% YTD vs ISRG US +12%. Medicaid work requirements in 2027 (CBO: 4.8M lose coverage) vs HCA's view that 2027 coverage loss is smaller than 2026.

reasoning: Continuation with an unlimited budget; same primary-document lane. Fundamentals from the filings are intact: Q2 revenue +19% to $2.89B, non-GAAP EPS $2.80, $8.63B cash, no debt, $4.7B buyback authorization. Several new primary-document findings were all negative or two-sided. (1) The 10-Q cash flow shows H1 OCF included a $370M deferred-tax swing, and management said the 31% FCF margin is a historical high vs a 22% average. Normalizing FCF cuts the DCF from $445 to ~$404. (2) The 2020 10-K confirms the prior EUP was modeled at $150-170M (~7% of I&A). The Q2 transcript shows BofA's ~5-point framework for 2027-28, and at Wells Fargo management called it 'directionally similar to 2020' with a 'gradual' net decline. So I now embed a 2-3% I&A/procedure drag in 2027 instead of ~1%. (3) The Ninth Circuit reversed the SIS judgment on 2026-08-13 and Intuitive sought en banc rehearing on 2026-09-28. Round 1 missed this; it strengthens the class action set for trial on 2027-09-14. (4) HCA's Q2 10-Q and call show elective surgical volumes falling and exchange admissions -15%, a real US headwind, though HCA expects 2027 coverage loss to be smaller. (5) J&J Ottava got De Novo authorization on 2026-07-22 for core general surgery. (6) The 2026 EPS consensus is $10.78, so my round-1 $11.15 was too high. On the bull side: the da Vinci 5 upgrade cycle (trade-ins 144 vs 83), SP +61% procedures, cardiac CE mark (Sept 22), China a small share (H1 2026 China tenders were only ~27 systems), Hugo not changing selling cycles yet, and only routine 10b5-1 insider sales. Valuation: P/E $412 (2028E $13.3 x 31x) and DCF $404 blend to $409, about 2% above spot. Scenarios at 25/50/25 give $295/$415/$545 (mean ~$418). Ladder: lognormal, median ~$410, sigma ~0.34 (near 37% realized vol), with a slightly fatter left tail for litigation, so P(>=401) is 0.525. The 1-month ladder tilts slightly negative into a tough-comp print after a 15% September rally. No option data was consulted; nothing under valuation/priors/ was opened.
